etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese 上ぐ (agu), following 下二段活用 (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”), from Proto-Japonic *ank-a-.
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From お (o, honorific marker) + 大(だい)事(じ) (daiji, “important”) + に (ni, particle for direction); shortened from expressions such as お大(だい)事(じ)になさってください (o daiji ni nasatte kudasai, “Please take care of yourself”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Perhaps from たとい (tatoi).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Derived as compound of どう (dō, “how”, question word) + も (mo, “ever, even, also”, particle). Literal meaning is close to “no matter how, howsoever, in all cases”. Idiomatically and semantically used as an intensifier in specific contexts. Compare とても (totemo, “very”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 丸 (maru, “round; (by extension) entirety”) + ごと (-goto).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English ski, from Norwegian ski.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 一(いっ)昨(さく)昨(さく) (issakusaku-, “the previous... before the last two...”) + 日(じつ) (jitsu, “day”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Compound of 先(さき) (saki, “previous”) + 一昨日(おととい) (ototoi, “day before yesterday”).
The kanji spelling is jukujikun (熟(じゅく)字(じ)訓(くん)).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Compound of 先(さき) (saki, “previous”) + 一昨日(おとつい) (ototsui, “day before yesterday”).
The kanji spelling is jukujikun (熟(じゅく)字(じ)訓(くん)).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
⟨maro₂⟩ → */marə/ → /maru/
Shift from Old Japanese 丸 (maro, see below).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Related to 麻(ま)呂(ろ) (maro).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
⟨maro₂⟩ → */marə/ → /maro/
From Old Japanese. Appears to be the older form.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/ɡwan/ → /ɡan/
From Middle Chinese 丸 (MC hwan).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 住(す)まう (sumau, “to live at; to dwell; to reside”).
First attested in the 970s.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 勤(つと)める (tsutomeru).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Cognate with Japanese 治(おさ)める (osameru) and 修(おさ)める (osameru).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: First attested in Shinsarugakuki (11th century) as 將基, but also later as 象戯 or 象棋 in other literatures. Probably cognate with Chinese 象棋 (xiàngqí).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 引き (hiki, the 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of verb 引く (hiku), “to pull”) + 出す (dasu, “to take out”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Calque of English tragedy, from Middle Chinese-derived elements 悲(ひ) (hi, “sad, sorrowful”) + 劇(げき) (geki, “drama; play”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 意識 (ʔiH syik).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese かふ (kapu), in the 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) pattern.
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.
Cognate with 変(か)える (kaeru), 替(か)える (kaeru) and 代(か)える (kaeru).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
*/uwu/ → /uweru/ → /ueru/
From classical verb 植う (uu).
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *takai.
Theories on derivation include:
* From 長(たけ)生(おう) (takeou) or 高(たか)生(はえ) (takahae), in reference to the speed at which bamboo grows.
* Cognate with 高(たか) (taka), 長(たけ) (take), 丈(たけ) (take), all “height”.
* From 高(たか)景(かけ) (takakake) or つらこえ (tsurakoe).
* From ta meaning “tall” (高(たか)い (takai)) + ke, ancient combining form of 木(き) (ki, “tree”).
* A contraction of 痛(いた)快(く)茎(き)延(は)へ (itakukihae), referring to the speed at which bamboo grows.
* From ta, from Korean 대 (dae, “bamboo”) (see also 대나무 (daenamu, “bamboo”, literally “bamboo tree”)), + ke, ancient combining form of 木(き) (ki).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 締(し)め切(き)る (shimekiru). By surface analysis, 締(し)め (shime, “fastening, locking, shutting”) + 切(き)り (kiri).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *mata. Cognate with Miyako 股 (また, mata), Okinawan 股 (また, mata).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese. First appears in the Kojiki of 712 CE. In turn from Proto-Japonic *kəsi.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 腰 (MC 'jiew).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 自然 (shizen, “nature”) + 科学 (kagaku, “science”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Reduplication of 色(いろ) (iro, “colour; type; kind”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese. First attested in the Kojiki of 712 CE. From Proto-Japonic *pukoro.
Very likely related to 含む (fukumu, “to include”), also among others deriving from a root *puk- (e.g. 膨れる (fukureru, “to swell”)).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 詩 (MC syi).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Middle Chinese 造船

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/t͡ɕɨu/ → /ɕjɨu/ → /ɕuː/
From Middle Chinese 周 (MC tsyuw).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 長 (“long; elder”) + 女 (“woman; female”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 隙(すき) (suki, “gap”) + 間(ま) (ma, “space”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 飛(と)び (tobi, “jumping”, the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 飛(と)ぶ (tobu, “to jump; to fly”)) + 込(こ)む (komu, “to go into”).
